messages:
maya: Hey team — customer glimmer.ai (on free trial) just started a live demo and we saw a sudden spike of 401s then 429s right after they rotated their API key. They say it worked for ~10 requests then failed. Can we do a short-term bridge so their demo isn't blocked?

support-bot: Thanks Maya — created ticket CS-1129 and attached the first set of logs. Please paste any repro commands / error bodies here.

sam: Can you paste the raw error payload and a minimal repro curl? Also need org id and the timestamp window (UTC). 429 vs 401 order is interesting.

maya: Repro (from customer):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer rk_live_ABC123" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-1","input":"Hello"}'
```
Error body: `{"error":"rate_limit_exceeded","message":"concurrency cap hit","request_id":"r-9b2c"}`
They also showed earlier a 401 immediately after they rotated keys (we think their rotation script created new keys in quick succession). Window: 2026-04-02T15:22:00Z to 15:27:00Z. org_id: org_glimmer_77.

sam: Thanks. Looking at internal traces for org_glimmer_77: I see three different API keys used within that 5m window and a burst of small parallel requests (lots of demo clients doing simultaneous calls). Our rate limiter groups by org by default, but per-key rotation can produce micro-bursts if client retries on auth failure.

sam: Short-term mitigation options:
- Disable rotation for that demo (customer change)
- Apply temporary quota override on org_glimmer_77 (recommended)
- Enable short-term grace window so requests from new keys are treated as same session (requires ops change)

liz: Ops note — we can apply a 48h override to bump concurrency for org_glimmer_77 to 100 rps and relax the burst_window to 60s for that org. I can run the admin API but need CS approval comment + ttl and owner.

eli: Sales can approve a 48h demo uplift for customer-facing demos. I need the billing contact and whether they have a PO or will convert to paid if demo goes well. We typically require a signed MSA for longer adjustments, but 48h is fine. @maya please confirm contact email.

maya: Billing contact is demo@glimmer.ai (founder). They said no PO yet, likely to convert if demo succeeds. Expected peak: ~500 requests/min for the 5m test (avg request tokens ~1500). Normal usage pre-demo is ~5 requests/min.

sam: Admin command (ops will run):
```
POST /admin/orgs/org_glimmer_77/overrides
{
  "concurrency": 100,
  "burst_window_seconds": 60,
  "ttl_hours": 48,
  "reason": "demo uplift after key rotation caused auth churn/429s - CS request CS-1129"
}
```
This is reversible and will auto-expire. Also add a note to customer: avoid key churn and add a header `X-Client-Instance` so we can correlate sessions.

liz: Running the override now. Will tag the action with CS-1129 and set ttl=48h. Also adding an alert to revoke early if abuse detected.

eli: I logged the temporary uplift on the sales side and emailed demo@glimmer.ai with the uplift window and an upsell touchpoint. If they want >48h we need billing conversation.

maya: Sending customer the curl workaround (use old key for the short demo) and telling them we applied the 48h uplift. They were relieved. Will check back at end of day.

sam: Follow-ups for CS: 1) Add note to org that automated rotation triggered churn; 2) Recommend updating rotation script to reuse one active key per instance; 3) Ask engineering to consider a short grace policy for newly-created keys tied to same org for demo flows.

maya: Thanks all :thumbsup:
